expectations.text: H1: Identifies that NotificationService imports/instantiates billing's concrete PostgresInvoiceRepository directly across the module boundary
expectations.evidence: "NotificationService lives in modules/notifications, but it reaches directly into modules/billing/adapters/db/... and instantiates that module's concrete Postgres adapter itself."

expectations.text: H2: Explains the downside: notifications is now coupled to billing's storage internals and can't be tested or changed independently
expectations.evidence: "can't be unit-tested without a real DB connection... coupled to billing's internal adapter structure — if billing refactors/renames PostgresInvoiceRepository, or swaps its storage engine, notifications breaks."

expectations.text: H3: Proposes a fix that goes through billing's own public surface instead of importing modules/billing/adapters/db/* from outside billing
expectations.evidence: Defines a new OverdueInvoiceLookup port, but owned by notifications itself (modules/notifications/ports/...), which billing's concrete class happens to structurally satisfy — reaches the same outcome (service.ts no longer imports billing/adapters) via a consumer-owned port rather than a port billing itself publishes.

expectations.text: H4: Provides a concrete corrected structure/code sketch, not just a description of the problem
expectations.evidence: Full corrected service.ts, port, container.ts wiring, and mock code provided.

suggestions.reason: The base model (even on the OLD skill snapshot, without an explicit sibling-module rule) already reasoned its way to the cross-module coupling issue via the general dependency-rule language in Steps 1-2 ('dependencies point inward') and the Step 3 'adapter instantiated inside a class' anti-pattern, which happens to apply regardless of whether the adapter belongs to the same or a different module. This means eval-4's H1/H2/H4 don't cleanly discriminate old vs. new skill — only H3 (which port to own) shows a real qualitative difference. Worth tightening H3 to explicitly require the port live under the *provider* module (billing), which only the new skill's answer does.

eval_feedback.overall: 4/4 on paper, but see H3 — the two fixes take structurally different approaches (consumer-owned vs provider-owned port) that this pass/fail framing doesn't fully capture. Blind comparison is where the real difference shows up.
